question: Why do ordinary forms of reasoning fail to reach Śiva?
premises: All parts of reasoning can operate without touching self-awareness.
Without self-awareness, reasoning lacks its highest ground.
Śiva is the final fruit only when that ground is reached.
inference: Therefore reasoning that does not touch self-awareness does not attain Śiva as its final fruit.
plain_english: For all the parts of reasoning that do not touch self-awareness never, anywhere, attain Śiva as their final fruit.
